newsitem.title: CHINA: China says 97 foreign borrowing cap set at $18 bln.
newsitem.headline: China says 97 foreign borrowing cap set at $18 bln.

text.p: China plans to have foreign borrowings capped at a preliminary $18.0 billion this year compared with a cap of about $16 billion last year, State Planning Commission officials said on Thursday.
They told Reuters that a cap of $12 billion would be set on central government mandated borrowings, up from $11 billion last year.
Borrowings that were "guided" by the central government, which include corporate borrowings guaranteeed by the government, would be at $6 billion versus $5 billion last year.
The official said the State Council, or cabinet, approves the government mandated loans while the State Planning Commission has control over the government guided funds.
Guided borrowing levels were somewhat more flexible, and credits could actually exceed the level set by government planners, he said, without elaborating.
The China Business Times said China would try to favour its less developed western and central regions in allocating foreign credits.
China is trying to close the income gap between the fast-growing coastal regions and western and central areas.
China this year would try to expand the use of BOT (build, operate and transfer) projects, seeking to use them for bridges, tollroads and power plants, the newspaper said.
This would allow foreign companies to build infrastructure projects in return for the opportunity to operate them for a period of time before handing them over to the Chinese government.
This has been widely seen as stimulating both direct investment as well as foreign lending.
